brief: A cabinet of three cells with two drawers, one of them shown pulled open.

requirements.evidence: Three full hex bases in a straight row at q=-1, 0, 1 (r=0, level 0): piece:-1,0,0, piece:0,0,0, piece:1,0,0.
Two drawer frames (family notch, hex-drawer-frame-notch fm and mf) placed in empty positions beside the touching bases, at (0,1) and (0,-1). Both accepted by the configurator with no clashes.

setNotchOpen open:true applied to the notch at (0,1) k1, the front drawer; the rear notch at (0,-1) stays closed. The configurator accepted it, but I did not visually confirm the pull-out with a look.

finish.summary: Built a three-cell cabinet: three full hex bases in a row, two notch-frame drawers (front one opened, rear one closed), with open faces capped and joints locked. check_build reports no issues and meshClash is clear. No props added since the brief did not ask for them. The drawer open state was set through the configurator and not visually confirmed.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
